intro.title: useMediaQuery
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a Vue component that dynamically responds to changes in the browser's viewport size. You will learn how to use the Composition API's reactive state and lifecycle hooks to create a custom `useMediaQuery` composable. This involves working with the `window.matchMedia` API to detect media query matches and updating the UI accordingly. By the end, you'll have a functional component that displays different messages based on whether the screen is in 'mobile' or 'desktop' mode.
intro.usecase: The useMediaQuery pattern is essential for building responsive interfaces that adapt to different screen sizes and user preferences. In real software products, developers use it to toggle navigation menus between desktop and mobile layouts, adjust dashboard panel arrangements, or change form input styles based on viewport width. For example, an e-commerce site might hide a sidebar filter panel on small screens or switch a video player to fullscreen mode when the device orientation changes. This allows developers to create seamless, adaptive UIs that improve user experience across devices.
